name: Audit signed packages and fund vendors
summary: Before the company pays a dealer for leased equipment, a funding specialist audits the signed package against the credit approval: signatures and guarantees, the vendor invoice and serial numbers, the security registration, insurance and a verification call confirming the customer received and accepted the equipment. Exceptions go back to dealers, brokers or credit; new vendors are verified by call-back and set up by someone who does not fund deals; a second person approves every payable and treasury releases the payment. Missing or wrong documents, undelivered equipment and unreachable customers cause most of the delay.

baseline.org_archetype: A privately owned Canadian independent equipment lessor with 340 staff funding about 1,400 small- and mid-ticket contracts a month through dealers, brokers and direct sales.
baseline.notes: Funding team of 11 funding and booking specialists, 3 registration clerks and a supervisor under the manager of documentation and funding. Treasury releases vendor EFTs from the bank portal once a day.

trigger: A complete signed document package is placed in the funding queue; the vendor invoice, registration confirmation and insurance status arrive separately and often later.
end_state: The vendor payment has been released by treasury, the partner notified and the funded file handed to booking, or the deal is cancelled or declined at funding.

volume.seasonality: Peaks in the last week of each month and quarter as partners push deals to fund, and in spring; low in late December. Low end reflects 2020, high end 2022.

evidence.note: Organisation file process map and the contracts-funded demand driver. In the simulation about 92% of files entering funding are paid; with about 1,490 signed packages a month from document preparation, that gives about 1,380 fundings, consistent with the driver.

Organisation file role, cost and headcount (11); cost consistent with the Job Bank NOC 14201 Ontario median loaded by 1.35 and scaled to 2019-2022. About 8 FTE on funding audits; the other 3 book contracts. Hands-on time implies about 8.6 FTE (see assumptions).
Organisation file role; share of time on funding approvals is an author estimate.
Organisation file role; large-funding approvals are an author estimate.
Organisation file role; funding exceptions are an author estimate.
Organisation file role; vendor master maintenance assigned here is an author assumption.

systems.name: Vendor and broker application portal with origination workflow and document generation
Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
Document imaging and contract file store
Provincial personal property registry and Quebec RDPRM search and registration portals
Commercial and consumer credit bureau portals (Equifax, PayNet)
Contact centre telephony and shared mailboxes

steps.name: Signed package enters the funding queue
steps.description: When the documentation team files a complete signed package, the origination portal moves the deal to the funding work queue, ordered by the date the documents arrived and flagged if the dealer asked for same-day funding.

evidence.note: Author estimate of portal queueing common in the period.

steps.name: Assemble the funding file
steps.description: A funding and booking specialist opens the file and gathers everything needed for the audit on two screens: the approval and its conditions from the portal, the signed documents and vendor invoice from imaging, the registration verification from the registration clerks and the insurance status from the insurance tracker. Missing items are noted before the audit starts.

evidence.note: Funding review of a package of documents is described; minutes and queue time are author estimates (most files are picked up the same business day).

steps.name: Audit signed documents against the approval
steps.description: The specialist checks each document against the approval: the agreement and schedule are signed by an authorised officer, every guarantor signed, initials and dates are present, amounts, payment, term and serial numbers agree across documents, the delivery and acceptance certificate is signed and the pre-authorised debit form has banking details. Defects go on an exception list.

error.defect_description: A missing guarantor initial or a payment mismatch between schedule and debit form is missed.

control.basis: Credit policy and funder eligibility criteria: no funding until signed documents match the approval and every condition is met

next.condition: defects the partner or customer can cure
condition not met, approval expired or structure changed

evidence.note: Signed-document and acceptance requirements from ELFA; missing signatures and wrong amounts in broker paper from Pawnee. The 22% first-pass exception rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Match the vendor invoice to the documents
steps.description: The specialist compares the vendor invoice with the documents and approval: it is made out to the company, the equipment description and serial numbers match the schedule, the price and taxes agree with the financed amount, any trade-in or down payment is shown and soft costs are within policy. A higher price or different unit is an exception.

error.defect_description: An inflated invoice or a serial number mismatch is not spotted.

control.basis: Funding policy: pay only against an invoice to the company that matches the financed equipment and amount

next.condition: invoice missing, not to the company or details differ

evidence.note: Fraudulent invoice creation is a named fraud type (ELFA Foundation); payment of equipment cost plus tax to the vendor is described. Shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Log exceptions and send cure requests
steps.description: The specialist records each exception in the portal and emails the dealer, broker or account executive a stipulation list: missing signatures or pages, corrected invoice, insurance certificate, or a registration amendment or prior-lender waiver. Registration corrections go to the registration clerks.

error.defect_description: Stipulation list incomplete, causing a second round.

evidence.note: Author estimate of exception handling common to lessor funding desks.

steps.name: Partner, vendor or customer cures the exceptions
steps.description: The dealer, broker or customer sends the missing pages, a corrected invoice or the certificate, often after the customer re-signs through e-signature or the vendor reissues the invoice. Some deals are cancelled at this point because the customer changed its mind or the equipment fell through.

next.condition: cannot be cured, needs a credit decision

evidence.note: Back-and-forth with brokers on deficient paper stretched funding from days into weeks (Pawnee); elapsed range and shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Re-check the cured items
steps.description: When cures arrive, the specialist checks only the items on the exception list: the re-signed page, the corrected invoice, the certificate or the amended registration. A fully re-signed package gets a complete re-audit; otherwise the file resumes where it stopped.

error.defect_description: A cure that only partly fixes the defect is accepted.

next.condition: document or invoice cures cleared, resume at vendor check

evidence.note: Author estimate of how funding desks re-check cured items rather than re-auditing the whole file.

steps.name: Credit decides on the funding exception
steps.description: A small-ticket credit analyst reviews the exception, such as a guarantor who will not sign, an approval older than its validity period needing a refreshed bureau, or a higher price, and waives it, adds a condition or declines the deal at funding. Decisions are recorded in the portal under the analyst's delegated authority.

control.basis: Delegated credit authority: only credit may waive or change approval conditions

evidence.note: Author estimate; the organisation file lists the credit analyst in this process.

steps.name: Look up the vendor record and banking
steps.description: The specialist checks that the vendor on the invoice is an approved vendor in the lease system with verified banking details on file. Dealers in a vendor program are already set up; one-off vendors on broker and direct deals, and any vendor that sent new banking instructions, need verification.

next.condition: new vendor or changed banking instructions

evidence.note: Processing vendor approvals by researching and validating information is described; share of new vendors is an author estimate.

steps.name: Verify a new vendor and its banking by call-back
steps.description: The specialist confirms the vendor exists from the corporate registry and its website, calls it on a number found independently (not the one on the invoice or email) to confirm the invoice and banking details, and obtains a bank letter or void cheque. Mismatches or pressure to pay quickly are treated as fraud flags.
outputs: verified vendor details or fraud flag

error.defect_description: A spoofed banking change is accepted.

control.basis: Payment fraud controls: independent call-back verification of new vendors and banking changes

evidence.note: Calling vendors directly to verify legitimacy (ELFA webinar); 76% of organisations targeted by business email compromise in 2020 (AFP). Minutes and waits are author estimates.

steps.name: Set up the vendor and banking in the lease system
steps.description: An operations analyst who does not fund deals enters the verified vendor and its banking details in the lease system's vendor master and attaches the bank letter, so the payable can be created.

error.defect_description: Account number keyed wrongly, causing a returned EFT.

control.basis: Internal control over payments: whoever maintains vendor master data does not approve or release payments

evidence.note: Vendor master maintenance and payment release as a segregation conflict (Sikich); assigning it to the operations analyst is an author assumption consistent with the organisation file.

steps.name: Check the registration and search results
steps.description: The specialist opens the registration verification statement and compares debtor names, serial numbers and collateral description with the documents, checks it was filed in the right province within the purchase-money window or, in Quebec, that the lease was published, and reviews the search for earlier registrations that need a waiver or discharge.

error.defect_description: A debtor name variance is accepted.

control.basis: Provincial PPSA (lease over one year; unperfected interest ineffective against a trustee; purchase-money priority if perfected within 15 days) and Civil Code of Quebec art. 1852 publication

next.condition: registration error or prior conflicting registration

evidence.note: Rules from the BC PPSA and the ELFA Quebec compendium; the check is company practice. Shares and minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Confirm insurance evidence or protection program enrolment
steps.description: The specialist checks in the insurance tracker that a certificate naming the company as loss payee is on file or that the customer will be enrolled in the protection program. Trucks and mid-ticket equipment need the certificate before funding.

control.basis: Lease terms and funding policy: equipment insured with the company as loss payee, or protection program enrolment

evidence.note: Author estimate; the organisation file has insurance tracking send an insurance confirmation to this process.

steps.name: Verbal verification call to the customer
steps.description: The specialist calls the customer on the number in the credit file, confirms they are speaking to the signer, and asks whether the equipment was delivered, is working and is accepted, and confirms the vendor, payment amount and term. Notes go in the portal. A vendor on the line, a different equipment location or pressure to rush are fraud flags.

error.defect_description: Call made to a number supplied by the vendor.

control.basis: Funding policy: lessee acceptance confirmed by signed certificate and verbal verification before funding

next.condition: customer not reached or equipment not yet delivered

evidence.note: Verification calls before funding are described by ELFA and a lessor's help centre. Shares and minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Wait for delivery or for the customer to call back
steps.description: The file waits until the equipment is delivered and installed or the customer returns the call. Specialists retry from a daily follow-up list; equipment delivered from the manufacturer or needing installation can take a week or more.

next.condition: customer cancels or equipment not delivered

evidence.note: Vendor is paid after the customer receives and accepts the equipment; elapsed range is an author estimate.

steps.name: Calculate the funding amount and enter the payable
steps.description: The specialist works out the amount to pay: equipment cost plus tax, less any down payment or first and last payments the vendor collected, less holdbacks, and splits it when there are several vendors. They enter the vendor payable and any broker commission in the lease system.

error.defect_description: Down payment not deducted or holdback missed, so the vendor is overpaid.

evidence.note: Payment of equipment cost plus tax to the vendor is described; deductions and minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Complete the funding checklist and route for approval
steps.description: The specialist ticks the funding checklist in the portal (documents, invoice, registration, insurance, verification, payable) and routes the file for a second signature: a peer funder for small files, the funding supervisor for larger files, exceptions and new vendors.

next.condition: larger file, exception waived or new vendor

evidence.note: A checklist of documents needed to release funds is described; routing thresholds are author estimates.

steps.name: Peer second review of the funding
steps.description: Another funding specialist reviews the checklist, the payable amount against the invoice and documents and the verification notes, and approves the payable in the lease system or returns it.

control.basis: Internal control over payments: a payable is approved by someone other than the person who prepared it

evidence.note: Separating origination and authorisation of a payment (Sikich); minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Funding supervisor approves the funding
steps.description: The funding supervisor reviews larger files, waived exceptions and new-vendor files, checks the payable and the verification, and approves in the lease system. Fundings above $250,000 are passed to the manager.

control.basis: Payment approval limits: supervisor approval above the peer-approval threshold

evidence.note: Author estimate of a common two-level approval matrix.

steps.name: Manager approves a large funding
steps.description: The manager of documentation and funding reviews mid-ticket fundings above $250,000, checks that credit conditions and any third-party payments are in order, and approves.

control.basis: Payment approval limits: manager approval for large fundings

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Release the approved payable to treasury
steps.description: The specialist sets the contract to funded pending payment, which places the approved vendor payable and broker commission in the treasury payment queue for the next EFT file; treasury releases payments from the bank portal, so funding staff never release cash.

control.basis: Internal control over payments: payment release by treasury, separate from funding approval

next.condition: lease system error blocks the payable

evidence.note: Separation of payment approval and release (Sikich); the organisation file sends the funding approval to treasury's daily cash process.

steps.name: Confirm the payment and send the funding notice
steps.description: After treasury's daily EFT run, the specialist checks the payment report, then emails the dealer or broker a funding notice with the amount and remittance details so they can release the equipment or close the sale.

evidence.note: Funding within 48 hours of signed documents and vendor payment in 2 to 5 days are advertised; the daily batch timing is an author estimate.

steps.name: Refer suspected fraud to the fraud analyst
steps.description: The specialist puts the file on hold and writes a referral to the fraud and verification analyst describing the flags, such as banking that does not match the vendor, a customer who did not know about the lease, or equipment at another address.

evidence.note: Fraud types and checks described by ELFA; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Act on the fraud review outcome
steps.description: When the fraud analyst clears or declines the file, the specialist either resumes funding, with vendor set-up if the flag was on the vendor, or closes the deal as declined and tells the partner it will not fund.

evidence.note: Author estimate; the fraud review is a separate process in the organisation file.

steps.name: Log an IT ticket and work around a system error
steps.description: When the lease system rejects the payable or the contract status will not change, the specialist logs an IT ticket with screenshots and, once IT fixes the data or configuration, re-releases the payable.

evidence.note: Author estimate; the organisation file sends IT tickets from this process.

steps.name: File the funded contract and hand it to booking
steps.description: The specialist indexes the final funded file in imaging, sends paper originals to the vault and moves the contract to the booking queue with the payment reference.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

exceptions.name: Deficient signed documents
exceptions.description: Missing signatures, guarantor pages or initials, or amounts that differ between documents; sent back to the partner and re-audited.

exceptions.name: Invoice problems
exceptions.description: Invoice missing, not made out to the company, wrong serial numbers or a higher price; the vendor reissues it.

exceptions.name: Credit exception at funding
exceptions.description: Condition not met, approval expired or price above tolerance; credit waives, re-conditions or declines.

exceptions.name: New vendor or changed banking
exceptions.description: One-off vendors and banking changes are verified by independent call-back and set up by the operations analyst.

exceptions.name: Equipment not delivered or customer unreachable
exceptions.description: The verification call cannot confirm acceptance; the file waits for delivery or a callback.

exceptions.name: Suspected fraud
exceptions.description: Banking, identity or equipment flags send the file to the fraud analyst; about a third are declined.

exceptions.name: Registration error or prior lien
exceptions.description: Debtor name or serial number errors need an amendment, or an earlier registration needs a waiver or discharge.

exceptions.name: Prefunding or progress payment
exceptions.description: Custom or manufactured equipment needs a deposit to the vendor before delivery; funded on an interim agreement with manager approval and later re-audited at acceptance. Not modelled as separate steps.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from signed package in the funding queue to vendor payment released or file closed, all outcomes
benchmarks.population: Canadian small- and mid-ticket equipment lessor, 2019-2022 (composite estimate)

evidence.note: Composite: Canadian lessors advertise funding within 48 hours of signed documents and vendor payment usually within 2 to 5 days of acceptance; deficient broker paper stretches funding from days into weeks, which sets the p90.

benchmarks.population: AFP 2021 Payments Fraud and Control Survey respondents (US treasury and finance professionals)

evidence.note: Stated in the AFP article; context for vendor banking verification.

benchmarks.unit: share of funding files with at least one document exception at first audit

evidence.note: No published figure found; set from descriptions of deficient broker paper (Pawnee) and common lessor experience.

pain_points.description: About one in five signed packages fails the first audit for missing signatures, pages or mismatched amounts, and each cure takes a day or more with the partner.

evidence.note: Deficient broker paper described; rate is an author estimate.

pain_points.description: Verification calls often fail because the customer is busy or the equipment is not yet delivered, so files wait days after documents are signed.

evidence.note: Funding waits for acceptance; frequency is an author estimate.

pain_points.description: Vendor invoices arrive late or wrong (not made out to the company, missing serial numbers), and invoice fraud and banking-change scams require slow manual call-backs.

evidence.note: Fraudulent invoices and business email compromise described.

pain_points.description: Payments wait for treasury's once-a-day EFT run, so a file approved after the cut-off is paid the next business day.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: Month-end peaks fill the funding queue as partners push volume, lengthening queue waits and approval waits.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

sources.title: Equipment acceptance is important
sources.publisher: Equipment Leasing and Finance Association (Equipment Leasing Today)
sources.supports: Lessors generally do not fund until the signed delivery and acceptance certificate is received; where the lessee has not signed a follow-up certificate after delivery, a prudent lessor requests one or makes a telephone verification call; deemed acceptance and pre-authorised funding before acceptance carry more risk.

sources.title: Your first 30 days (customer help centre)
sources.supports: A verification call is when a member of the lessor's documentation team calls an approved applicant to confirm they applied for the financing and received the equipment; a cover letter serves as the checklist of documents needed to release funds; customers then receive a welcome letter.

sources.title: 5 takeaways from ELFA webinar on fraud detection, mitigation and prevention
sources.supports: Lenders should call vendors directly to verify they are legitimate and consider a physical inspection for pricier equipment to verify it exists; email, address, device and IP checks of the originating party.

sources.title: New Foundation study examines the prevention, detection and impact of fraud on the equipment finance industry
sources.supports: Fraud types in equipment finance include identity theft, use of legitimate credentials by criminals, first-party fraud by owners, impersonation and fraudulent invoice creation; incidents of some types rose 10% or more over two years; preventive checks are more effective than investigation; many firms do not track fraud losses.

sources.title: Credit Coordinator, Bennington Financial Corp (job posting)
sources.publisher: EQ Bank / EQB Inc. on Lever
sources.supports: A Canadian equipment lessor prepares preliminary credit packages for the funding review, collecting the documents needed to finalise the credit audit at funding, and processes vendor approvals by researching and validating information.

sources.title: Personal Property Security Act [RSBC 1996] chapter 359
sources.supports: Section 3: the Act applies to a lease for a term of more than one year; section 20: an unperfected security interest is not effective against a trustee in bankruptcy; section 34: a purchase-money security interest has priority if perfected within 15 days after the debtor obtains possession.

sources.title: State law compendium: Quebec, publication
sources.supports: Civil Code of Quebec article 1852: rights under a lease of more than one year of a road vehicle or of movable property needed to operate an enterprise must be published to be set up against third persons; late publication is effective only from its date.

sources.title: AFP survey: payments fraud increase attributed to coronavirus pandemic (2021 Payments Fraud and Control Survey)
sources.supports: 74% of organisations were targeted by payment scams in 2020; 76% were targeted by business email compromise; 62% of those with attempted or actual fraud said it came from business email compromise.

sources.title: Why segregation of duties is a key internal control and how to implement it
sources.supports: Segregation of duties splits originating, authorising, recording and reconciling a transaction; maintaining vendor master data and releasing payments is a conflict; dual authorisation of payments above thresholds in the payables system and bank portal.

sources.title: Toronto equipment financing
sources.supports: Once approved and documents are signed, funding and equipment release typically happen within 48 hours for standard leases.

sources.title: What we lease (vendor leasing process)
sources.supports: Canadian vendor leasing sequence: signed agreements returned, release or purchase order to the vendor, delivery, customer receives and accepts the equipment, then the vendor is paid the equipment cost plus tax usually within 2 to 5 days.

sources.title: Pawnee Leasing Corporation achieves 50% faster access to capital with DocuSign eSignature (case study)
sources.supports: Broker-submitted agreements often arrived with missing signatures or wrong amounts, causing repeated back-and-forth and funding delays that stretched from days into weeks.

sources.title: Wages: Financial clerk, financial sector in Ontario (NOC 14201)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low $18.00, median $25.48, high $35.90 (2023-2024).

assumptions: The case starts when the signed package reaches the funding queue. Triggered_by shares give the input whose arrival usually starts or restarts the audit: signed documents in most cases, the vendor invoice or registration confirmation when they arrive last, and a fraud clearance for files re-entering after review.

Lessors were not FINTRAC reporting entities in 2019-2022 (organisation file assumption), so verification and fraud checks rest on company policy, funder eligibility and fraud risk, not on anti-money-laundering law.

Every payable needs a second person: a peer funder for small files, the funding supervisor for larger files and exceptions and the manager above $250,000; treasury releases the EFT. Thresholds are author estimates.

About 92% of files entering the funding queue are paid; about 8% are cancelled before funding (mostly undelivered equipment or customers changing their minds), declined at funding by credit or declined for fraud. Cases per month keep the process map figure of 1,400 although slightly more files enter than fund.
External steps have zero touch time; customer, vendor and partner time is in wait_before_min.

Funding specialists split their time with booking (book-contracts), so fte_on_process is about 8 of 11, with 3 on booking. Hands-on time implies about 8.6 FTE here and about 4.5 FTE in booking, roughly 13 FTE against 11 people before any registration support, so the organisation file appears to understate the funding team by one or two people (or the team relies on overtime at month end).
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (2019-2022 wage times 1.35).
